family.tagline: A greenhouse with sensors, and a house that reads them.
family.story: Amani is a firmware engineer who builds the sensors in the family greenhouse. Freya teaches primary school, and her class plants the same seeds every spring. Their greenhouse log lives on one Companion Core.

companion.name: Kip
companion.job: Reads Home Assistant sensor values and tells Amani what changed.
companion.limits: Reports only. Amani decides what to change.

companion.name: Pernille
companion.job: Opens Grist in its own browser and logs what the class planted.
companion.limits: Logs what Freya reads out. She checks it.

popup.title: A long walk to the library
popup.body: The parcel arrives in the foyer. Freya carries it past the living room and down the hall to the library. Amani has cleared the desk.

popup.title: Baraka reads the guide aloud
popup.body: Baraka, visiting for the week, opens the parcel and reads the quick-start guide aloud. Also inside: the Companion Core, a power cable and a recovery USB drive.

popup.title: Press once, then wait
popup.body: Amani presses the button once the cable is in. The Core wakes and opens its own Wi-Fi network.

popup.title: Freya joins, Amani supervises
popup.body: Freya joins the Core's own network from her phone. Amani watches over her shoulder as she picks the home network.

popup.title: Two agents, three apps
popup.body: In Companion Hub, Amani picks Hermes and Freya picks OpenClaw. They add Home Assistant, Grist and ntfy, then walk out to inspect the greenhouse.

beats.capability: Hermes runs in its own sandbox on your Core and talks to you through the messaging platform you pick

popup.title: Kip asks which sensor
popup.body: Amani sends the first message to Kip, the agent he named. Kip answers, and the Core is running.
popup.note: Messages pass through the chat service you choose.

say.speaker: amani
say.text: Hello, Amani. Kip here. Which sensor first?

beats.capability: One start page for every app on your Core

popup.title: The TV opens on the Core
popup.body: Homarr gives the wall TV a start page. It holds a tile for each app on the Core, and one for the greenhouse readings.

beats.capability: Back up, search and organise your family photos and videos on your own Core

popup.title: Seedlings, pictured every morning
popup.body: On the couch, Baraka sends his morning seedling pictures to Immich. They are backed up to the Core, ready to search.

beats.capability: Take notes and keep to-dos that sync across your devices through your own server

popup.title: Lesson notes, synced at home
popup.body: At the farmhouse table, Freya writes Monday's lesson notes in Joplin Server. They sync to her laptop and her phone through the Core.

beats.capability: Control and automate your smart home from one place, locally, without a cloud account

popup.title: Kip reads the overnight values
popup.body: Over coffee, Amani asks Kip what changed in the greenhouse. Kip reads the Home Assistant values and reports. Amani decides.

say.speaker: amani
say.text: Overnight report ready. You decide the changes.

beats.capability: Track the pantry, shopping lists, recipes, chores and household habits in one place

popup.title: Harvest in, shopping list shorter
popup.body: Tuesday's salad comes from the greenhouse. Freya logs the harvest in Grocy, so the shopping list leaves out the lettuce.

beats.capability: Run a quiz night for a small group on your own Core

popup.title: Quiz night on the Core
popup.body: Friday is quiz night. Freya writes the questions, Amani runs Razzia from the breakfast bar, and Baraka defends his title.

beats.capability: Chat with models running on your own Core, from any browser

popup.title: Datasheets, explained locally
popup.body: Amani asks the model in Open WebUI to explain a sensor datasheet in plain words. The model runs on the Core, and he checks the answer against the page.

beats.capability: Block ads, trackers and bad domains for every device on your network at the DNS level

popup.title: Ads and trackers, blocked at DNS
popup.body: Amani points the home network's DNS at Pi-hole. His sensors, the phones and the laptops all ask the Core first, and ads and trackers get blocked.

beats.capability: A collaborative wiki for notes and documentation

popup.title: One manual page per sensor
popup.body: Amani documents every sensor he builds in Docmost, one page each. The wiki sits on the Core, where the sensors report.

beats.capability: Save web pages with a screenshot and PDF so they survive link rot

popup.title: The datasheet page, saved for good
popup.body: Amani saves a datasheet page in Linkwarden, with a screenshot and a PDF. The copy survives if the original page disappears.

beats.capability: Assign and track household chores and recurring tasks, with NFC tag completion

popup.title: Tap the tag, laundry done
popup.body: A tag on the washing machine marks the laundry chore done. Donetick keeps the rota for Amani and Freya.

beats.capability: Read Wikipedia and other reference sites offline

popup.title: How a seed sprouts, looked up
popup.body: At the writing desk, Baraka reads how seeds sprout in Kiwix. The pages come from a copy on the Core.

beats.capability: Manage and read books, comics and PDFs with automatic covers and metadata

popup.title: A comic before lights out
popup.body: Baraka reads a comic in BookLore before lights out. The covers fill in by themselves, and the whole library lives on the Core.

beats.capability: Control and automate your smart home from one place, locally, without a cloud account

popup.title: The vent opens by rule
popup.body: A sensor Amani built reports the greenhouse temperature. Past his set point, Home Assistant runs the vent fan.

beats.capability: Send a push notification to your phone from any script or automation with one request

popup.title: A cold-night note to the phone
popup.body: On a cold night, an automation sends a ntfy note to Amani's phone. He reads it and decides whether to cover the trays.

beats.capability: A spreadsheet-database with real Python formulas, stored as a SQLite file you can copy

popup.title: Pernille logs the trays
popup.body: Freya reads out what her class planted. Pernille opens Grist in its own browser and logs each tray. A formula counts the days. Freya checks every entry.

say.speaker: freya
say.text: Trays logged. Please check each entry.

beats.capability: Stream your own music collection to any device

popup.title: The patio gets a playlist
popup.body: On Sunday, Amani lights the grill and Freya queues her records on the patio. Navidrome streams them from the Core to the speaker.

popup.title: A house that reads its sensors
popup.body: A glass greenhouse, a library desk and a spare room for a visiting nephew. The Ochieng-Sorensen household runs it all from one Companion Core.

closing.body: Your sensors, your seed log and your lesson notes can live on a Companion Core at home. Start with one tray in Grist.

notes: Owner sign-off open: the FTUE hotspot flow is written as the owner specified and is not on the fact sheet (STORY-BIBLE section 15, item 1).

Home Assistant (kitchen-kip, green-vent): the Hub has no USB, Bluetooth or GPIO, so the sensors Amani builds are home-network devices that report over Wi-Fi. No energy or savings claim; the text never says which protocol they use.

ntfy (green-frost): iOS push goes through an upstream relay (catalog caveat), so the text says only that a note reaches his phone. Kip (Hermes) only reports; Amani decides. Hermes note sits on ftue-hello, the first Hermes beat.

Cast gave Pernille a HortusFox job. HortusFox is over the fleet cap, so only her job text changed, to Grist; name, runtime, voice and limits are as cast. No website is opened, so the OpenClaw web note is unused.
Razzia needs a manager password set at install (catalog caveat); the text says nothing about it. Linkwarden saves a page with a screenshot and PDF; no cloud claim is made.
Baraka is a visiting nephew aged twelve: three beats, never voiced, no companion. Freya's class is a school class; no school is named and no learning-outcome claim is made.
Joplin Server is named in full because the catalog entry covers the server only; the Joplin apps are separate.
Town Fenwick Prairie and street Cattail Lane are invented and still need the human map check.
